input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic delivers the keyboard accessibility fixes for the four core Dashboard
flows identified by the accessibility audit — project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission — so that each flow is
fully operable by keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable
controls, and consistent visible focus indicators. The audit report enumerates
the exact defects per flow; this epic resolves every enumerated defect.

## Scope

- Remediate all keyboard-operability defects the audit enumerated across the
  four audited flows:
  - project creation
  - workbench spawn
  - model deployment
  - pipeline run submission
- Eliminate focus loss and focus traps in the modals used by the audited
  flows (focus must return to the invoking control when a modal closes, and
  must remain within the modal while it is open).
- Make every interactive control in the audited flows reachable and operable
  via keyboard traversal.
- Apply consistent visible focus indicators across the audited flows, per the
  audit's indicator findings, so focus state is uniformly detectable.
- Add regression coverage (automated where practical, otherwise a documented
  manual keyboard-walkthrough checklist) for the fixed defects so the flows
  cannot silently regress.

Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require,
and flows outside the four audited ones (per the strategy's Out of Scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows can be completed end to end using keyboard
  input only, verified by a walkthrough against the audit report's defect
  list, with every enumerated defect for those flows marked resolved.
- No focus traps remain in the audited flows: focus contained within open
  modals and restored to the invoking control on close, verified per the
  audit's enumerated modal defects.
- No unreachable controls remain in the audited flows: every interactive
  control is reachable and operable by keyboard, verified per the audit's
  enumerated reachability defects.
- Focus indicators are visibly consistent across all controls in the audited
  flows, verified per the audit's indicator findings.
- Regression coverage for the fixed defects exists and passes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — The four audited core flows are fully operable by
  keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls: covered by the
  keyboard-operability, focus-trap, and reachability scope above.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows: covered by the focus-indicator scope above. Bundled with HLR-1
  because both are resolved by the same remediation sweep over the same UI
  surfaces enumerated by the audit; a separate epic would revisit every
  already-fixed surface.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
for the Dashboard — the VPAT conformance statement and the product
documentation's accessibility statement — so that it reflects the fixed state
of the four audited core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
deployment, pipeline run submission) after the keyboard accessibility
remediation is implemented. Two public-sector customers require the updated,
published conformance statement before renewal, so the published documentation
is a first-class deliverable of this work, not an incidental follow-up.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Update the VPAT so every criterion affected by the keyboard fixes reflects
  the corrected conformance level for the four audited flows, with support
  notes referencing the fixed behavior.
- Update the product documentation's accessibility statement to describe the
  current keyboard-accessibility state of the audited flows.
- Republish both documents through the Red Hat docs content process.
- Obtain and record technical review of the updated content against the
  implemented fixes before publication.

Boundary: the updated documents must claim conformance only for what the
keyboard fixes actually implement — screen-reader semantics beyond what the
keyboard fixes require and flows outside the four audited ones remain out of
scope per the strategy, and the VPAT must not assert conformance beyond that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to reflect the fixed state of the four audited flows,
  with each previously-failed criterion revised to its corrected conformance
  level and support notes matching the implemented behavior.
- The product documentation's accessibility statement is updated and
  republished.
- The updated content is technically reviewed against the implemented
  keyboard fixes, with the review sign-off recorded, before publication.
- The published documents make no conformance claims beyond the implemented
  fixes (no claims covering screen-reader semantics beyond the keyboard work
  or flows outside the four audited ones).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)** — The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review: covered in full by this epic's
  scope.
